findings.title: F1 — "creates new stack if original error has no stack" no longer has a stackless original
findings.quote: In `src/error/__tests__/GraphQLError-test.js:57-64` the fixture `const original = { message: 'original' }` was replaced with `const original = new Error('original')` so that the sixth constructor argument satisfies `?Error`. A real `Error` always has a `stack`, so the constructor now takes the `originalError && originalError.stack` arm at `src/error/GraphQLError.js:195` and copies the original's stack, which is the opposite of what the title says and exactly what the preceding test, `uses the stack of an original error` (lines 41-55), already checks with a stronger assertion. The two tests are now duplicates apart from `null` versus `undefined` placeholders, and the case the title names — an `originalError` is supplied but carries no stack, so `Error.captureStackTrace(this, GraphQLError)` must run — is no longer exercised anywhere. A scratch probe confirmed it: with the base fixture `captureStackTrace` is called once and `e.stack !== original.stack`; with the head fixture it is called zero times and `e.stack === original.stack`. The test still passes because its only stack assertion is `to.be.a('string')`, which holds on either arm. Keep the `Error` so the call type-checks, but make it genuinely stackless — `Object.defineProperty(original, 'stack', { value: undefined })` routes through `captureStackTrace` again in the same probe — after which the existing `to.be.a('string')` assertion means what the title claims; or, if the case is not worth keeping, delete the test rather than leave a weaker duplicate under a misleading name. Detail: [01_graphqlerror_test_fixtures.md](01_graphqlerror_test_fixtures.md).

findings.title: F2 — the `nodes` nullability fix is applied to one of two parallel constructor signatures
findings.quote: `src/error/GraphQLError.js` declares the constructor twice: the ambient `declare class` at lines 22-31, which callers are checked against, and the implementing `export function GraphQLError` at lines 92-100, which the body is checked against. The PR widens line 25 to `nodes?: $ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void | null` and leaves line 94 at `nodes?: $ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void`, so the file now states that `null` is both accepted and not accepted for the same parameter, seventy lines apart, with nothing in the toolchain relating the two. The body is null-safe, so this is a contract defect and not a runtime one, but it is the only line in the PR that ships (the file is copied to `dist` as the `.js.flow` definition) and it should not ship half-done. The spelling compounds it: every other nullable parameter in both lists uses the maybe prefix (`?Source`, `?$ReadOnlyArray<number>`, `?Error`), and the sibling at `src/type/validate.js:101` writes the same shape as `$ReadOnlyArray<?ASTNode> | ?ASTNode`, yet this change extends the one outlier to `| void | null`, the longhand for what `?` already means. Change both lines to `nodes?: ?($ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode)` so the two signatures agree and the parameter list reads uniformly. Detail: [02_graphqlerror_constructor_contract.md](02_graphqlerror_constructor_contract.md).

findings.title: F3 — an unexplained `$FlowFixMe` is added where a plain string literal removes the need for it
findings.quote: `src/jsutils/__tests__/inspect-test.js:31` gains a bare `// $FlowFixMe` above ``expect(inspect('"')).to.equal(String.raw`"\""`)`` so that the file can be marked `@flow strict`. The comment gives no reason, issue link or version tag, unlike the suppressions in `src/jsutils/objectValues.js:15`, `isInteger.js:14`, `isFinite.js:14` and `src/subscription/mapAsyncIterator.js:25`, and it blankets the whole following line, which includes the `inspect(...)` call the test exists to check — so on this line the PR turns the type-checker on and off again in the same commit. The tagged template is not earning its place: the expected value is four characters, and ``String.raw`"\""` `` is the same string as `'"\\""'` (confirmed at runtime). Replace the template with the literal and delete the suppression, which reduces this file's diff to the header line; if `String.raw` is kept for readability, give the suppression a reason and move it so it covers only the template. Detail: [04_inspect_test_suppression.md](04_inspect_test_suppression.md).

findings.title: F4 — the Flow narrowing in the two-source `printError` test is duplicated and misnamed
findings.quote: In `src/error/__tests__/printError-test.js:62-80` the base's two one-line lookups (`sourceA.definitions[0].fields[0].type`) became two identical three-line blocks — bind `opA`/`opB`, `invariant(op && op.kind === Kind.OBJECT_TYPE_DEFINITION && op.fields)`, bind `fieldA`/`fieldB` — followed sixteen lines after the first binding by a joint `invariant(fieldA && fieldB)`. The narrowing is pasted rather than shared, the proof that each field exists lives away from the binding it guards, and `opA`/`opB` name `ObjectTypeDefinitionNode`s with the abbreviation the sibling test file uses for operation nodes, apparently carried over from it. Extract one local helper that takes a body and a source name, performs the narrowing once with each invariant directly under its binding, and returns `field.type`; the test body then shrinks back to two calls and the `GraphQLError` construction, the `op*` names disappear, and the base's `fieldTypeA`/`fieldTypeB` vocabulary is restored. The `sourceA` → `docA` rename in the same hunk is correct and should stay. Detail: [03_printerror_and_located_tests.md](03_printerror_and_located_tests.md).
